bodleian:pococke-375-3b-4a.name: Muḥammad al-Idrīsī
bodleian:pococke-375-3b-4a.detail: His geographical work was copied into the Bodleian’s 1553 manuscript. Authorship of the work and production of this surviving copy belong to different dates.

bodleian:pococke-375-3b-4a.name: ʻAlī ibn Ḥasan al-Ḥūfī al-Qāsimī
bodleian:pococke-375-3b-4a.detail: Fihrist names this scribe in the description of the Naskh hand. The manuscript keeps the earlier author’s work in a later written copy.

loc:2007678037.name: Eadweard Muybridge
loc:2007678037.detail: The print credits Muybridge and explains the intervals at which its negatives were made.

loc:2007678037.name: Leland Stanford
loc:2007678037.role: Owner of the named mare in the caption
loc:2007678037.detail: The printed caption identifies Sallie Gardner as Stanford’s horse. It separately credits the photography.

cern:6qhcbugnq4rng.name: Tim Berners-Lee
cern:6qhcbugnq4rng.role: Used the original machine to develop and host the Web
cern:6qhcbugnq4rng.detail: The Science Museum’s CERN loan account identifies his NeXT computer as the one that hosted the first Web page.

cern:6qhcbugnq4rng.name: Mike Sendall
cern:6qhcbugnq4rng.detail: The Science Museum account identifies Sendall as the manager who approved purchase of the NeXT machine in 1990.

perkins:procede-1829.name: Louis Braille
perkins:procede-1829.detail: The first edition describes an adapted system for words and music, with dots and dashes. It is distinct from the later no-dash version.

perkins:procede-1829.name: Charles Barbier
perkins:procede-1829.role: Earlier contributor credited in the book
perkins:procede-1829.detail: Perkins notes that Braille acknowledged Barbier’s earlier tactile dot system while explaining how their systems differed.

perkins:procede-1829.name: Jen Hale
perkins:procede-1829.role: Perkins archivist who discussed the surviving copy
perkins:procede-1829.detail: Hale describes uncertainty about how the book reached Perkins. The article treats acquisition by Samuel Gridley Howe as a possibility.

harvard:a02969.name: Henrietta Swan Leavitt
harvard:a02969.role: Astronomer who marked and analysed the plate
harvard:a02969.detail: The Harvard comparison identifies her star marks on the back of the glass and shows their mirror relationship to her sky-facing chart in the notebook entry of 2 November 1906.

met:2005.100.931.name: John Moran
met:2005.100.931.detail: The Met credits Moran for this 1871 albumen print of the cathedral in Cartagena. The printed image and the mount have different recorded edges.

met:2017.69.28.name: José Negretti
met:2017.69.28.detail: The Met credits Negretti for this albumen print. Its framed vantage cannot supply the accounts of the people whose work the site depicts.

cma:1955.320.name: Maria Sibylla Merian
cma:1955.320.role: Artist credited for the published plate
cma:1955.320.detail: The Cleveland Museum credits Merian. Its date of 1771 describes this engraved impression, produced after her lifetime.

ypm:yu.009738.name: Rolla M. Tryon
ypm:yu.009738.role: Collector named on the herbarium record
ypm:yu.009738.detail: The Yale Peabody record names Tryon for this 1961 collection on the road to Hanover north of Zanderij.

us:3693365.name: W. D. Stevens
us:3693365.role: One of the four named collectors
us:3693365.detail: The specimen record names Stevens with O. Montiel J., C. Davidson and S. Christoph. It places this collection near a monument in Parque Nacional Cerro Corá.

us:3757218.name: E. Pasini
us:3757218.role: One of the three named collectors
us:3757218.detail: The U.S. National Herbarium identifies Pasini with F. Torchelsen and E. Hayden, and distinguishes their field number from the accession.
